title: The motel application, iv
logline: Thursday. Gully's. The news. Gully says 'nights' the way he says 'hm' under a hood. Maria says it's fine. The baby says nothing. The dog will have to sleep alone.

panels.composition: Gully's. WOOD on the stool. GULLY. MARIA with the baby, one, on her hip. BARNABY.

balloons.text: It's fine, Gully. It's a job.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, a thin man on a bait-shop stool, a stocky man in an apron, a practical woman with a baby on her hip, an old dog beneath the stool

panels.composition: Gully's face doing the thing it does under a hood.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, close-up of a stocky man's face making a small doubtful sound

panels.composition: Maria, handing the baby to Gully and taking Wood's cup to refill it. The head-shake. Not at Wood.

balloons.text: We've got the dog. Nights. He'll sleep by the register.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, a practical woman refilling a coffee while handing a baby to a man in an apron, giving him a small head-shake

panels.composition: The dog, under the stool, looking up at all of them deciding his nights. The baby looking at the dog.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, an old dog under a stool looking up at the people above it while a baby looks down at the dog, no words

art.line: brush-pen; the flats cleaner; the Sundays the point now

notes: 'We've got the dog. Nights.' Maria arranges it.
